originalTitle: Xbox is officially embracing the chaos of AI-powered game ports

content: Retro gaming is going through a wild time at the moment, thanks to decompilations and recompilations that are letting gamers port classic titles to new devices, or merge code from two different games into a single new experience. Microsoft has witnessed skateboarding being modded into Call of Duty and Halo being played in a web browser, and the company is now officially embracing the chaos of this new AI-powered era of game modding. Microsoft is putting together a new Xbox Labs group to explore the rapid emergence of these mods, many of which use AI models to help modders remix games in ways we’ve rarely seen before. Xbox Labs will be a “small group of game makers, engineers and scientists whose job is to turn emerging ideas into things our players and developers can experience,” says Xbox CEO Asha Sharma. “We’ll build in the open, learn from what people do, and measure success by whether more people are playing and creating.” Sharma thinks the experiments we’ve seen in recent weeks, where Windows PC builds have been translated to run on Apple Silicon or ported to run inside browsers, “challenge long-held assumptions about our industry: the tether between software and hardware, the boundary between creation and play, and how people discover and experience games.” “While it is hard to predict the future of gaming, it is easy to see the possibilities in making great games easier to access, giving old games new life and allowing more players to become creators and co-creators,” says Sharma. “These are unmistakably good outcomes for players, even when (and sometimes because) they challenge our existing business models.“ Modders are now doing the type of work that Microsoft has been doing for decades with its Xbox backward compatibility program, letting old games run on modern hardware. But they’re doing it without the business model restrictions that Microsoft is tied to. It’s starting to feel like we’re just a model or two away from even more breakthroughs that decouple more modern games from their intended hardware. Sharma clearly sees an opportunity here, particularly for AI agent use at Xbox. “I think Xbox has an important role to play here,” says Sharma. “Coding became the first major workload for agents because they can write, run, and test software. Games share many of those same properties, and people spend more than 72 billion hours a year playing XBOX games, roughly five times the estimated time spent writing code worldwide.” Xbox Labs is clearly a way for Microsoft to experiment with how AI will shape where games are played, and Xbox will share any tools and learnings with developers. The bigger question is how Microsoft will respond to decompiles and recompiles of games where modders take its precious IP and make it freely available. Modding is fun, but I can’t see Microsoft and other publishers seeing the fun side if modern console games start to appear where they shouldn’t. I asked Microsoft to comment about unauthorized IP use, but the company didn’t respond in time for publication. Here’s Sharma’s full memo: > Team, > The first video games emerged some 75 years ago. In the time since, there have been booms and busts, but every year there are more great games to play, more devices to play them, and best of all, more people than ever playing. That growth helped make XBOX what it is today, and we’ve helped shape the industry in return, from bringing hard drives to consoles and online gaming through Xbox Live to Game Pass and cloud gaming, alongside franchises that have brought millions of people together. > In recent weeks, we’ve seen games rapidly decompiled and rebuilt to run on hardware they were never originally designed to support. Windows PC builds have been translated to run on Apple Silicon or ported to run inside a browser through WebAssembly and WebGPU, the latter now approaching 90% global browser support. Perhaps more surprisingly, we’ve seen many of the biggest games in the world have been remixed into the source code of another. > These experiments challenge long-held assumptions about our industry: the tether between software and hardware, the boundary between creation and play, and how people discover and experience games. While it is hard to predict the future of gaming, it is easy to see the possibilities in making great games easier to access, giving old games new life and allowing more players to become creators and co-creators. These are unmistakably good outcomes for players, even when (and sometimes because) they challenge our existing business models.  To explore these possibilities, I’ve asked Scott to stand-up XBOX LABS, a small group of game makers, engineers and scientists whose job is to turn emerging ideas into things our players and developers can experience. We’ll build in the open, learn from what people do, and measure success by whether more people are playing and creating.  > I think XBOX has an important role to play here. Coding became the first major workload for agents because they can write, run, and test software. Games share many of those same properties, and people spend more than 72 billion hours a year playing XBOX games, roughly five times the estimated time spent writing code worldwide. We’ve spent 25 years learning how to make great games, and I want our game makers to help shape what these new technologies make possible. As we learn, we’ll share the tools we build with developers across the industry, just as we always have. > Our priorities aren’t changing. We remain committed to the 4Cs, to making great games, to our hardware and to being responsible stewards of IP and the communities built around it. LABS gives us a way to explore new technology without abandoning the work already underway. > Asha
chineseTitle: Xbox 正式拥抱 AI 驱动的游戏端口的混乱
chineseSummary: 复古游戏目前正在经历一段疯狂的时期，这要归功于反编译和重新编译，让游戏玩家可以将经典游戏移植到新设备上，或者将两个不同游戏的代码合并到一个新的体验中。微软见证了滑板被改装成《使命召唤》和《光环》，并在网络上玩[...]
chineseContent: 复古游戏目前正在经历一段疯狂的时期，这要归功于反编译和重新编译，让游戏玩家可以将经典游戏移植到新设备上，或者将两个不同游戏的代码合并到一个新的体验中。微软见证了滑板被改装成在网络浏览器中玩的《使命召唤》和《光环》，该公司现在正式接受这个由人工智能驱动的游戏改装新时代的混乱。微软正在组建一个新的 Xbox 实验室小组来探索这些模组的快速出现，其中许多模组使用人工智能模型来帮助改装者以我们以前很少见过的方式重新混合游戏。 Xbox 首席执行官阿莎·夏尔马 (Asha Sharma) 表示，Xbox 实验室将是一个“由游戏制作者、工程师和科学家组成的小团体，他们的工作是将新兴想法转化为我们的玩家和开发者可以体验的东西”。 “我们将开放地构建，向人们的行为学习，并通过是否有更多的人在玩和创造来衡量成功。” Sharma 认为，我们最近几周看到的实验（其中 Windows PC 版本已被转换为在 Apple Silicon 上运行或移植为在浏览器内部运行）“挑战了我们行业长期以来的假设：软件和硬件之间的联系、创作和游戏之间的界限，以及人们如何发现和体验游戏。” “虽然很难预测游戏的未来，但很容易看到让优秀游戏更容易访问、赋予旧游戏新生命以及让更多玩家成为创造者和共同创造者的可能性，”夏尔马说。 “对于玩家来说，这些无疑是良好的结果，即使（有时是因为）他们挑战了我们现有的商业模式。”模组制作者现在正在做微软几十年来一直在做的工作，即 Xbox 向后兼容计划，让旧游戏在模式下运行
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于 AI 与科技趋势信号，适合用于观察工具选型、产品机会、开发者关注点和技术路线变化。
